newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mostly down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mostly down.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat bids were mostly lower on Wednesday in line with weaker MGE wheat futures, dealers said.
MGE May spring wheat closed down 4-1/2 cents at $4.05 a bushel.
Lower prices again discouraged farm sales with many dealers reporting scant activity. About four inches of heavy snow has hit Montana which was good for pre-planting moisture, a Montana dealer said.
He expected farmers to start preparatory fieldwork for spring planting in a few more days.
"Between April 10-15, most farmers will begin to hit the fields for spring and barley," he said.

Also, warmer weather caused flooding in parts of South Dakota on Wednesday as runoff from melting snow spilled from rivers into low-lying areas. The long-range outlook for flooding was uncertain and will depend on temperatures and possible rainfall in the coming days, officials said.
